name: a sort on player_name orders the result rather than being dropped (executed-result parity)
description: player_name has no select_as, no column_name and a main_select returning bare strings, so every sort-resolution method in get-data-view-results returns null, select_position stays 0 and the sort is discarded in silence -- the query falls back to the trailing pid tiebreaker. Because a pid's letter prefix is built from the player's own name, pid order looks alphabetical and hides this. Seeded so the two orders disagree: pid ascending gives Zed Alpha, name ascending gives Aaron Zulu. Asserted through limit 1, since the harness sorts rows and cannot see order directly -- which row survives the limit is the observable consequence, and it is also what a paged view actually depends on. player_league_roster_status is unsortable for the same reason.
expected_query: select "player"."pid", player.first_name, player.last_name, "player"."primary_position" AS "primary_position_0", "player"."primary_position" from "player" where player.primary_position IN ('MLB') group by player.first_name, player.last_name, "player"."primary_position", "player"."pid", "player"."last_name", "player"."first_name", "player"."primary_position" order by player.first_name || ' ' || player.last_name ASC NULLS LAST, "player"."pid" asc limit 1
